articles.title: 6 Members of South Africa’s Biggest Party Are Killed in Shootings
articles.description: The two shootings took place only a few weeks before pivotal, nationwide local elections, and as the party, the A.N.C., is embroiled in a dispute over the eligibility of more than 100 candidates.

articles.title: 20 Hours After Falling Overboard, Cruise Passenger Is Rescued Near Greece
articles.description: According to Greek officials, the woman told her rescuers she had jumped off the ship because she “wanted to disembark.”

articles.title: Second Ebola Infection Announced in Kenya
articles.description: The case is likely to raise alarms in the country and increase scrutiny of the government’s surveillance measures.

articles.title: The Papers: 'Neets crisis is moral failure' and 'Credit crunch'
articles.description: PM brands Neets "crisis" a "moral failure" and cereal prices could rise in healthy food crackdown lead Monday's papers.

articles.title: EU tariffs aimed at China hitting Ukraine, steel boss says
articles.description: The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies says the country has been "bundled together" in measures aimed at curbing cheap imports.

articles.title: Don't fall for this - how to protect yourself from AI scams
articles.description: Trading standards officers say AI is "super-charging" existing scams through clones and fake websites.

articles.title: Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going
articles.description: The US president blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect.

articles.title: Major fire at Canada military base leaves four dead, dozens injured
articles.description: Prime Minister Carney said military and emergency crews fought the flames throughout the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable".

articles.title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day
articles.description: More property asking prices are being cut than at any time in 15 years, data shared with the BBC shows.

articles.title: France in Shock After Protests Turn Into Riots, Damaging Buildings and Shops
articles.description: After anti-government protests devolved into chaos, leaders from across the political spectrum blamed one another for the unrest, even as it largely subsided on Sunday.

articles.title: Albania’s Leader, Edi Rama, Denounces Violent Protests
articles.description: Students upset by living and educational costs have revived protests. Prime Minister Edi Rama said they were being used by “outside forces.”

articles.title: Venezuela’s Opposition Leader Calls Trump’s New Oil Partner Corrupt
articles.description: The businessman denied accusations made by María Corina Machado in a wide-ranging interview, in which she promised to return to Venezuela “sooner than you would expect.”

articles.title: Inside Chicago's battle against the synthetic drugs flooding the US
articles.description: The BBC's Quentin Sommerville reports from Chicago, where communities are battling a new wave of synthetic drugs.

articles.title: Planet Earth and Brazil’s Election
articles.description: The Amazon rainforest has been a crucial battleground in the country’s presidential runoff.

articles.title: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
articles.description: French President Emmanuel Macron gives a national address after widespread disorder and as some looting continued in Paris.

articles.title: Madueke's 'anger and conviction' shows he's more than a 'finisher'
articles.description: Noni Madueke may not have the role he wants at Arsenal but his winning goal against Nottingham Forest showed why he is one of Mikel Arteta's valued players.

articles.title: Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27
articles.description: Presley Gerber's death in September is being investigated as a suspected overdose.

articles.title: Sage feels 'shame' at Palace thrashing with future in doubt
articles.description: Crystal Palace manage Pierre Sage says he feels "shame" at the Eagles' performance during their 5-0 thrashing by Brighton and does not know if he will be given time to save his job.

articles.title: Shades of Barca and Beckham - Brighton aim to maintain superb start
articles.description: With 23 goals in seven Premier League matches, including some stunning strikes, Brighton continue to delight their fans and get them dreaming of what might be.

articles.title: Northampton beat Cardiff for only English win of Champions Cup openers
articles.description: Northampton edge to a nervy Champions Cup pool win against tenacious Cardiff at Franklin's Gardens.

articles.title: Hearts roll out red carpet ... and Celtic walk all over it
articles.description: Hearts thought attack was the best form of defence at Celtic Park. They were badly wrong, writes Tom English.

articles.title: Kenya Confirms Four New Ebola Cases
articles.description: Seven Ebola infections have now been confirmed in Kenya, which before this month had never recorded cases of the deadly virus.

articles.title: Mbeumo offers Carrick solace as Man Utd winless run goes on
articles.description: Michael Carrick said he had his headphones on this week so didn't hear the noise around Manchester United, but a 1-1 draw at Leeds means it is six games without a win.

articles.title: The French City of Limoges Wasn’t Known for Unrest. Then Rioters Set Fire to Its City Hall.
articles.description: As unrest surged across France this weekend, the most surprising attack came in the quiet city of Limoges, where rioters set fire to the city hall.

articles.title: Deadly ‘Incident’ at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright Sparks Fire
articles.description: The defense minister said people were killed and injured at a base in Alberta, but officials did not offer details on the cause.

articles.title: Pope Leo Leaves Hospital, Days After Lung Cancer Surgery
articles.description: Leo XIV had been treated for lung cancer at Gemelli Hospital in Rome.

articles.title: Unrest Mars Day of Protest in France, as Student Movement Turns National
articles.description: Riots broke out in several French cities alongside peaceful marches of tens of thousands of people demonstrating against rising living costs and poor school conditions.

articles.title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked
articles.description: A misconduct hearing said many of the records accessed were sensitive and held "intimate information".

articles.title: Egypt’s Defense Chiefs Pledge to Support Saudi Arabia After Houthi Attacks
articles.description: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi had called on Egyptian lawmakers to authorize military assistance to the kingdom, saying any support would be defensive.

articles.title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion
articles.description: The Green Party leader said, while he wanted to amend it, the motion would stand until 2028.

articles.title: Zelensky Says Trump Risks ‘Historic Mistake’ If He Backs Russia
articles.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine pressed Sunday for more information on possible restrictions to Starshield, a U.S.-provided satellite internet service used by the Ukrainian military.

articles.title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme
articles.description: The BBC said all journalism and editorial decisions are made by BBC journalists and editors.

articles.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
articles.description: An expedition to a remote Pacific island hoping to uncover the American aviator's wreckage was on hold for three days.

articles.title: Britain's Kartal misses out on biggest title of her career
articles.description: Britain's Sonay Kartal fades from a strong position in a gripping Wuhan Open final against Grand Slam runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

articles.title: In India, the Scion of a Political Dynasty Tries to Seize His Moment
articles.description: Rahul Gandhi is the descendant of three prime ministers. A surge of protests could give him a springboard to take on the nation’s current leader.

articles.title: Suspects hunted after police officer injured in shooting
articles.description: A firearm has been recovered by officers after a man and a woman fled the scene, detectives say.

articles.title: Watch: Pope thanks well-wishers in first event after cancer surgery
articles.description: The Pope's first event since his lung cancer diagnosis and surgery saw him recite the traditional Angelus prayer from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace.

articles.title: At Least 19 Dead After Stampede at Indian Religious Event
articles.description: Such deadly crowd events are relatively common in India, and it was unclear what caused this one. The authorities detained the event’s organizer and others involved.

articles.title: Israeli Settlers Attack Palestinians and European Officials in West Bank
articles.description: Extremists assaulted residents and broke a European diplomatic vehicle’s window, witnesses said, as settler violence surges in the territory during the olive harvest.

articles.title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
articles.description: BBC News hears from users, dealers, prison and recovery workers as the country battles with a deadly new drug epidemic.

articles.title: Dispute Between Trump Allies Centers on Millions Transferred From Congo
articles.description: The White House inquiry is focused on diverging accounts from Richard Grenell and Alina Habba Mildon about a $17 million transfer from a government account in the African country to a Texas defense firm.

articles.title: Mexican Judge Sentences 3 Men to 159 Years Each in Surfer Killings
articles.description: The men were charged in the murders of two Australians and an American who were on a camping and surf vacation in Mexico.

articles.title: What to Know About the Violent Protests in Albania
articles.description: Student demonstrations over education converged with broader protests against rising living costs and a luxury development linked to Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law.

articles.title: Egypt’s President Says He Will Leave Office in 2030
articles.description: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, who has so far ruled for over a dozen years, pledged to respect constitutional limits while also seeking parliamentary approval to help defend Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: U.S. Floats Lifeline to Russia: Allowing More Gas Sales to Europe
articles.description: The Trump administration is pitching the idea as part of a peace deal with Ukraine, but Europe is wary and critics say Russia would be strengthened.

articles.title: Deadly School Roof Collapse in Pakistan Raises Questions Over Regulation
articles.description: A teacher and 32 children were killed in northwest Pakistan in an episode has prompted safety inspections of schools across the region.

articles.title: The World’s Oldest Shipwreck? Maybe, but ‘We’re All Excited by Maybe.’
articles.description: Archaeologists said that they had found jars from a shipwreck as much as 4,700 years old, with black residue inside. Outside experts were skeptical but intrigued.

articles.title: Uncertainty Over Pope’s Health Fuels Familiar Debate Over Vatican’s Candor
articles.description: By announcing his lung condition himself, Leo has been more forthcoming than many popes. But mysteries remain, prompting scrutiny of papal statements for hidden meaning.
